title: Orchestrate node draining and rolling upgrades for Dedicated fleets
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Goal: Implement an automated, observable, and safe node lifecycle system for Dedicated fleets that handles scheduled maintenance, draining, rolling upgrades, and maintenance windows while preserving throughput guarantees and cooperating with autoscaling policies. Background: Dedicated customers run fixed GPU pools with throughput SLAs. Current maintenance (kernel/driver/runtime upgrades, node reprovisioning) is manual and causes variable capacity loss and long tail latency spikes. We need a deterministic node lifecycle controller plus a host agent to coordinate drain windows, eviction policies, and graceful rejoin so upgrades have minimal customer impact. This work spans control-plane orchestration, host-agent changes, autoscaler integration, Console controls (maintenance windows), and runbook + telemetry for SRE/Customer success.
acceptance_criteria: Controller exposes a node lifecycle API with states: SCHEDULED, CORDONED, DRAINING, DRAINED, UPGRADING, REJOINING, ACTIVE
Automated drain flow preserves at least 95% of committed throughput for pools with >= 5 nodes (measured over a 5-minute window) by ramping replacements via the autoscaler before eviction
Draining respects per-tenant priorities: high-priority workloads are migrated before low-priority ones; eviction order is configurable via policy
KV cache/Session cache treatment defined: option to snapshot cache metadata, or allow pre-warm of replacement nodes to keep tail latency increase < 20% for 95th percentile during upgrades
Maintenance window scheduler in Console allows defining weekly blackout windows and one-off maintenance events; UI shows projected capacity impact and suggested autoscaler overrides
End-to-end tests validate: cordon -> drain -> upgrade -> rejoin across AZs with no request loss and with tracing showing graceful request migration
Runbook and postmortem checklist added for failed drains and rollback scenarios
Metrics/alerts: drain_duration distribution, percent_capacity_remaining_during_maintenance, drain_failures, upgrade_rollout_progress; dashboards added to Console release
Documentation updated: API spec, host-agent config, recommended autoscaler settings, operator runbook

notes: Trade-offs discussed: slow drains reduce request churn but lengthen maintenance windows; to hit SLA targets we will default to spawning replacements ahead of drain for pools >=3 nodes and fall back to drained-only for pools of size 1-2 with customer notification

Implementation plan: (1) control-plane lifecycle controller + CRD-style API, (2) lightweight host agent to quiesce new connections and report drain progress, (3) autoscaler hook to pre-provision replacements, (4) Console maintenance scheduler and simulation mode, (5) e2e tests and canary on non-critical customers
Telemetry: add trace tags to requests migrated during drain (node_from/node_to) for latency attribution; expose drain_time_per_node metric

Fallbacks: if drain fails due to stuck long-running requests, controller can either (a) extend drain with alert, (b) escalate to force-evict after configurable timeout, or (c) postpone upgrade. Default policy: extend once + alert to SRE.
Open questions: How to treat pinned KV caches for ultra-low latency customers? Proposal: allow 'no-drain' flag with SLA penalty and manual approval (managed via Console and contract).
